explain.say: Imagine a family of elements so content that they almost never join in. Those are the noble gases: helium, neon, argon and friends, in group 0. Look at the board, and you will see why they are so calm.

explain.say: See the first reason? Neon's outer shell has 8 electrons, so it is completely full. Helium's tiny shell is full with just 2. Remember, other atoms react to fill their outer shells. So what do you think a noble gas needs to do?

explain.say: Nothing at all! Look at the next reason. With a full shell, there is no need to gain, lose or share electrons. So we call them inert, which means they do not react. Why might that be useful to you?

explain.say: Look at the uses on the board. Helium is lighter than air and cannot burn, so it fills party balloons. Neon glows red-orange in signs. Argon guards hot metal during welding. Which of these have you seen?

Wonderful! One more secret: argon makes up almost 1 percent of the air you are breathing right now. Wow: in 1962, a scientist finally made a noble gas react, forming the first compound of xenon. Even the calmest elements have limits!

faq.a: Their outer shell of electrons is already full, so they do not need to gain, lose or share electrons. That makes them very stable.

faq.q: Why is helium used in balloons?
faq.a: Helium is much less dense than air, so balloons float, and unlike hydrogen it cannot burn, so it is safe.
asks: Why not use hydrogen in balloons?

faq.a: When electricity passes through neon gas, its atoms gain energy and then give it out as red-orange light. Other gases give other colours.

faq.q: Why are noble gases single atoms?
faq.a: Because their shells are full, they do not bond to each other. They exist as separate single atoms, unlike oxygen, which pairs up as O2.
Very rarely. In 1962 the first compound of xenon was made, and some xenon and krypton compounds with fluorine are now known. Helium and neon have no stable compounds.

facts: Argon makes up about 0.93 percent of dry air.
The first noble gas compound, containing xenon, was made by Neil Bartlett in 1962.
